- Introduction: State the problem of comparing composite and conventional electrodes in electrical discharge machining (EDM) of Hastelloy, explain why this comparison matters for machining Hastelloy components, and list the study's objectives and scope as currently known. Do not include literature review, experimental details, or results here; do not claim objectives or hypotheses that are not present in the project scope.
- Literature Review: Organize prior work on EDM and electrodes into the themed sections below, for each theme establish what is known about EDM behavior, electrode materials, and machining of corrosion-/heat-resistant alloys like Hastelloy, and identify gaps that justify this thesis. End the chapter with a concise statement of the gap this thesis addresses. Do not present the thesis methodology or results here.
  - EDM process fundamentals and key parameters: Summarize the fundamental physics and commonly studied process parameters in electrical discharge machining as they relate to material removal, surface generation, and electrode wear; identify which parameters are most relevant for experiments on Hastelloy and electrode comparison. Do not present experimental data from this thesis.
  - Electrode materials: conventional versus composites: Review prior studies comparing conventional electrode materials and composite electrodes in terms of conductivity, thermal properties, manufacturability, and expected wear in EDM; note which material properties are hypothesized to affect machining of Hastelloy. Do not assert untested performance advantages for any electrode type.
  - Fabrication and characterisation of composite electrodes: Cover methods used to produce and characterise composite electrodes (microstructure, homogeneity, electrical/thermal measurements) with attention to measurements needed before EDM tests on Hastelloy. Do not include the thesis' own fabrication or measurement results.
  - EDM of Hastelloy and related nickel-based alloys: Collect evidence on the machinability of Hastelloy and closely related nickel-based corrosion/heat-resistant alloys under EDM, focusing on material removal rate, surface integrity, recast layer, and difficulties encountered. Do not extrapolate findings beyond the alloy class without cited support.
  - Performance metrics and measurement methods for EDM studies: Describe common performance metrics used to compare electrodes in EDM (e.g., electrode wear, MRR, surface roughness, recast thickness, tool degradation) and the measurement techniques appropriate for Hastelloy specimens. Do not prescribe a specific analysis protocol for the thesis—reserve that for Methodology.
  - Synthesis and research gap: Synthesize the preceding sections to state precisely what is established and what remains unknown regarding composite versus conventional electrodes when machining Hastelloy, and define the specific gap this thesis will fill. Do not include experimental findings from this thesis in the gap statement.
- Methodology: Describe and justify the experimental design, sample preparation, electrode types (composite and conventional), EDM parameter selection, measurement instruments, and analysis methods so another researcher could repeat tests comparing electrodes on Hastelloy. For each objective in the study scope, state which measurements and analyses will address it. Do not present results or interpretive claims here.
  - Experimental design: Specify the overall experimental plan: number of trials, controlled variables, factor levels for EDM parameters, electrodes compared, and which outcomes are primary versus secondary. Do not report experimental data or outcomes.
  - Samples and electrode preparation: Detail Hastelloy specimen geometry and preparation procedures, and the fabrication/selection and pre-test characterisation of composite and conventional electrodes. Do not include test results or performance data.
  - Machining setup and EDM parameters: Report the EDM machine configuration, dielectric, spark/pulse settings, flushing strategy, and how parameter values were chosen and justified relative to the objectives. Do not present outcomes from machining runs.
  - Measurement instruments and procedures: List and justify the instruments and measurement procedures for electrode wear, MRR, surface roughness, recast layer thickness, and microstructure (e.g., microscopy, profilometry), including calibration and uncertainty estimation. Do not include measurement results.
  - Data analysis and statistical methods: Explain the data processing steps, statistical tests, error analysis, and criteria for significance used to compare composite and conventional electrodes, and map each analysis to the corresponding objective in the scope. Do not present analyzed results.
  - Reproducibility, limitations and safety: State procedures to ensure repeatability and reproducibility (replicates, randomisation), identify expected methodological limitations, and record safety precautions specific to machining Hastelloy and handling electrodes. Do not discuss experimental outcomes.
- Results: Report the experimental findings comparing composite and conventional electrodes on Hastelloy: raw and processed data for electrode wear, material removal rate, surface roughness, recast layer and relevant micrographs and tables. Present results objectively and map each result to the objective it addresses. Do not interpret the findings or compare them to the literature beyond labelling which objective they answer.
- Discussion: Interpret the results in light of the literature themes from the Literature Review, explain whether and how each objective was met, discuss practical implications for EDM of Hastelloy, and state limitations honestly. Do not introduce new data; where limitations exist, specify how they affect conclusions.
- Conclusion and Future Work: Answer the study objectives in order using the evidence from Results and Discussion, state the thesis contribution about composite versus conventional electrodes for EDM of Hastelloy, and propose concrete next steps or follow-up experiments that address the study's limitations. Do not repeat detailed data tables or analyses.

- Introduction: Establish the problem of corrosion of maraging steel produced by selective laser melting (SLM): why corrosion performance of SLM maraging steel matters for components and which performance gaps motivate this thesis. State the working title and precisely define the technical scope (material: maraging steel; manufacturing route: SLM; phenomena: corrosion behaviour). List the study aims and note where formal research objectives must be inserted if they are not yet specified in the project documentation. Do not present literature review material or any results here.
- Literature Review: Review prior work organised by sub-theme relevant to corrosion of maraging steel made by SLM, state what each theme has established and what remains uncertain, and finish by stating the specific gap this thesis will address. Do not report experimental data from this thesis in this chapter.
  - Corrosion mechanisms in maraging steels: Summarise mechanistic understanding of general corrosion, pitting and intergranular attack in maraging and high-strength martensitic steels, and identify which electrochemical processes and microstructural features control susceptibility. Do not discuss additive-manufacturing-specific microstructures here except to highlight where mechanisms may differ.
  - Effects of selective laser melting on microstructure: Survey how SLM processing (thermal cycles, layer-wise melting and rapid solidification) alters microstructure, defects (porosity, lack of fusion), texture and residual stress in maraging alloys and related steels, and state how these microstructural changes could plausibly affect corrosion. Do not present new micrographs or results from this thesis.
  - Influence of alloying and heat treatment on corrosion: Review how composition and subsequent ageing/solution treatments of maraging steels modify precipitate populations, hardness and corrosion resistance, and note which post-processing protocols have been evaluated for SLM-produced maraging alloys. Do not prescribe a heat-treatment schedule for this thesis in this section.
  - Localized corrosion, pitting and crevice behaviour: Compile findings on pitting initiation, propagation and crevice corrosion in martensitic and maraging steels, emphasising microstructural initiation sites relevant to SLM features (pores, unmelted particles, interfaces). Do not interpret the current thesis data here.
  - Corrosion testing methods for additively manufactured metals: Compare immersion tests, electrochemical techniques (EIS, potentiodynamic polarization), accelerated salt/fog exposure and surface analysis methods used to assess corrosion of AM metals; evaluate advantages and limitations of each for SLM maraging steel. Do not present the methods chosen for this thesis as the only valid approaches.
  - Protective coatings and mitigation strategies: Summarise studies that investigated coatings, surface modifications and process controls to mitigate corrosion in maraging and SLM steels, and identify which strategies remain under-investigated for SLM maraging steel. Do not propose a final solution for the thesis here.
- Methodology: Describe and justify the overall experimental design so another researcher could reproduce the study on SLM-produced maraging steel. For each specific research objective named in the project documentation, state which experimental or analytical procedure will address it; if objectives are not yet provided, list the measurements and analyses that will answer common objectives for corrosion studies of SLM maraging steel. Do not present results in this chapter.
  - Study design: Define the comparative groups (as-built SLM samples, various heat-treated conditions, and any reference wrought maraging steel), sample counts and the repeatability strategy; justify sample sizes and controls with respect to measuring corrosion metrics.
  - Materials and sample fabrication: Describe powder specification, SLM machine and build environment, and sample geometry so fabrication can be repeated; do not include fabrication results here.
    - Powder feedstock and SLM parameters: Specify powder chemistry and morphology and the chosen SLM parameter set (laser power, scan speed, hatch spacing, layer thickness) that will be used and why these were selected.
    - Sample geometry and pre-build preparation: Describe sample shapes and sizes for electrochemical and immersion tests, surface finishing procedures, and any machining or polishing steps before testing.
  - Heat treatment and post-processing: Describe the ageing, solution or tempering schedules to be applied to subsets of samples and justify choices in terms of microstructural targets (precipitates, hardness). Do not report microstructural outcomes here.
  - Corrosion testing protocols: Define the immersion, salt spray and electrochemical test procedures (electrolyte composition, temperature, exposure durations, scan rates) that will be used to assess corrosion behaviour and why each is appropriate for SLM maraging steel.
    - Immersion tests: Specify immersion media, exposure times, mass-loss or visual-inspection criteria and how corrosion rates will be calculated from immersion data.
    - Electrochemical tests: Describe EIS, open-circuit potential monitoring and potentiodynamic polarization protocols including cell geometry, reference electrode and data acquisition parameters.
  - Microstructural and electrochemical characterisation: List microscopy, phase analysis and surface-chemistry techniques to be used to link microstructure to corrosion behaviour and justify each technique's role in answering the research aims.
    - Optical and electron microscopy: State which metallographic, SEM and (if planned) TEM observations will be performed to characterise porosity, grain structure and precipitates and how samples will be prepared.
    - EIS and potentiodynamic polarization: Explain how EIS and polarization data will be acquired and modelled to extract corrosion parameters (e.g. charge transfer resistance, corrosion current).
  - Data analysis: Specify statistical methods, uncertainty estimation and criteria for significance; describe how electrochemical and mass-loss data will be combined to produce corrosion-rate metrics and how microstructural metrics will be correlated with corrosion outcomes. Do not present analysed numbers here.
- Results: Report the empirical findings of the SLM maraging steel study clearly and objectively, using tables and figures for microstructure, porosity, hardness, electrochemical measurements and mass-loss/visual inspection outcomes. Organise results so each subsection maps to one method in the Methodology chapter and to the corresponding research objective; do not interpret results or compare them to the literature here.
  - Sample fabrication and microstructure: Present data on achieved SLM build quality, porosity measurements, optical/SEM images, and quantitative microstructural descriptors (grain size, texture, precipitate presence) without interpretation.
  - Heat-treatment effects on structure and hardness: Report changes in microstructure, hardness and phase fractions after each heat-treatment condition tested, with supporting figures and tables.
  - Corrosion test outcomes: Provide raw and processed results from immersion and accelerated exposure tests (mass loss, visual ranking, pit counts) organised by sample condition.
  - Electrochemical measurements: Show EIS spectra, fitted circuit parameters, potentiodynamic curves and derived corrosion currents and potentials for each sample group.
  - Summary of quantitative findings: Provide concise tables and figures that collate the principal quantitative results (corrosion rates, statistical comparisons, microstructure–property correlations) to prepare for interpretation in the Discussion.
- Discussion: Interpret the results in relation to the literature reviewed in Chapter 2 and the study aims stated in Chapter 1, explaining how each major finding answers the corresponding research objective. Discuss mechanistic links between SLM-induced microstructure/defects and observed corrosion behaviour, compare with prior studies, and state limitations and alternative explanations honestly. Do not repeat raw data tables; refer to them instead.
  - Interpretation against prior work: Compare each key result (e.g. corrosion rates, pitting tendency, effect of heat treatment) with findings from the Literature Review and explain agreements or discrepancies.
  - Mechanisms linking SLM microstructure to corrosion: Integrate microstructural observations and electrochemical evidence to propose mechanisms by which SLM features (porosity, residual stress, precipitates) influence corrosion initiation and propagation.
  - Limitations and alternative explanations: State methodological, sampling and measurement limitations (e.g. sample size, representativeness of SLM parameters, test duration) and discuss how they might affect the conclusions; propose how future work could resolve these uncertainties.
  - Implications for manufacture and component design: Discuss practical implications of the findings for SLM process selection, post-processing and design decisions for parts made from maraging steel, without providing prescriptive industrial specifications.
- Conclusion and Future Work: Answer the stated research objectives in order and concisely summarise the thesis contribution to knowledge about corrosion behaviour of SLM-produced maraging steel. If the formal objectives are missing from project documentation, explicitly list the objectives used to generate these answers. End with a prioritized list of concrete next steps for research and for industrial follow-up. Do not introduce new data or new literature here.

- Introduction: Establish the research problem: why rural households delay rooftop solar adoption in India, who is affected (specificly rural households in India), and the study's geographic and temporal scope. State the study aims and the exact research questions or objectives as they will appear in this thesis (do not invent objectives—report the ones listed by the student). Do not review literature or present results here.
- Literature Review: Review prior work organized by the thematic barriers and enablers relevant to rooftop solar adoption by rural households in India, and end by identifying the specific empirical gap this thesis will address. For each theme say what is established, what is contested or weak, and why that leaves a gap for this study. Do not present the study's methods or findings here.
  - Economic barriers and affordability: Summarize evidence on up-front costs, financing options, payback perceptions, and perceived affordability as they pertain to rural Indian households delaying rooftop solar adoption. Identify what is known and where evidence is thin or inconsistent for rural settings. Do not propose new policy solutions yet.
  - Information, awareness and trust: Review studies on awareness of rooftop solar technology, trust in vendors and programmes, and the role of information diffusion in rural India. Highlight gaps in measured information channels and trust metrics specific to rural adopters versus urban adopters. Do not report this thesis's empirical findings here.
  - Policy, subsidies and institutional barriers: Assess evidence on the effect of central and state policies, subsidy schemes, administrative procedures, and utility interactions on household rooftop adoption in India, with attention to rural implementation challenges. Note where evaluations lack rural disaggregation or causal identification. Do not restate policy rules in full detail.
  - Technical capacity and grid/infrastructure constraints: Cover literature on roof suitability, grid connectivity, net-metering, and maintenance capacity in rural contexts and how these technical factors delay adoption. Point out missing empirical measures of technical readiness at village or household level. Do not include original technical survey results.
  - Socio-cultural and household decision factors: Review household decision-making dynamics, gender roles, social norms, and risk preferences that influence rooftop solar uptake in rural Indian households, and identify where evidence is limited. Do not extrapolate from non-comparable populations without noting limits.
  - Local markets, supply chains and vendor behaviour: Examine the role of local suppliers, installation capacity, after-sales service, and informal finance markets in rural rooftop solar adoption, noting evidence gaps about vendor practices and rural service coverage. Do not repeat content from the economic barriers section; focus on market- and supply-side evidence.
- Methodology: Describe and justify the research design, sampling frame, data sources, instruments, and analytical methods that will allow another researcher to repeat the study of why rural households delay rooftop solar adoption in India. For each stated objective in the Introduction, explain exactly which data and analysis steps will answer it. Do not present results here.
  - Design and sampling: Specify the study design (cross-sectional, longitudinal, mixed methods, etc.), sampling universe (which states/districts/villages and household selection rules), and sample size calculations or justification; state clearly what geographic and population exclusions apply.
  - Data sources and instruments: List and justify primary and secondary data sources, survey modules, interview guides, and any technical measurements (roof suitability, system specs); include how instruments were piloted and how missing data will be handled.
  - Analysis methods and identification: Describe statistical and qualitative analysis methods (regressions, causal identification strategy, thematic coding), robustness checks, and how each method identifies the causal or descriptive claims the thesis will make. State pre-analysis plans or registration if used.
- Results: Report empirical findings about why rural households delay rooftop solar adoption in India, organized to answer the research questions listed in the Introduction. Present descriptive statistics, regression tables, qualitative themes, and figures as appropriate. Do not interpret the results or compare them to literature in this chapter.
- Discussion: Interpret the results in relation to the themes in the Literature Review: state which hypotheses are supported and which are not, explain plausible mechanisms, and compare to prior findings about rural adoption barriers in India. Explicitly state the study's limitations (sampling, measurement, identification) and avoid overstating generalisability beyond the sampled rural populations and contexts.
- Conclusion and Future Work: Answer the research questions or objectives in the order they were presented in the Introduction, summarise the thesis contribution about delays in rooftop solar adoption by rural households in India, and propose concrete next steps for research and policy. Do not introduce new empirical results or literature here.
